# Google Ads for Yoga Studios: Setup and Budget Guide

Part of the guide: [Fitness Studio Google Ads](https://datalatte.pro/guides/fitness-ads)

May 16, 2026·Nataliia Rumiantsewa· 9 min read [All posts](https://datalatte.pro/blog)

On this page▼

Google Ads can fill yoga classes by showing your studio to people searching "yoga near me", "beginner yoga classes \[city\]" or "hot yoga \[neighborhood\]" at the moment they are ready to book.

A sensible first test is one Search campaign, a radius around your studio sized to how far students will travel, an intro-offer landing page, and conversion tracking for calls and bookings. Fund it for at least two months, set the budget from what a new student is worth, and judge it by cost per sign-up.

WordStream by LocaliQ's 2026 benchmarks put Health and Fitness at $6.17 per click, a 5.81% click-through rate, $67.36 per lead and a 6.94% conversion rate. There is no separate yoga row, so treat these as a rough range and replace them with your own account data after the first month.

See Sources at the end of the article. Cards marked Assumption are examples, not results.

## What Can $600 a Month Buy?

**Every input below is an assumption, not a market benchmark. Swap in your own numbers.** Assumption: a $600 monthly budget, the click prices and sign-up rates in the table, 40% of intro students joining, and a member paying $120 a month who stays 6 months (lifetime value $720).

|     | A: base case | B: clicks cost double | C: weak landing page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cost per click (assumption) | $3  | $6  | $3  |
| Clicks ($600 / cost) | 200 | 100 | 200 |
| Click-to-intro sign-up rate (assumption) | 5%  | 5%  | 2%  |
| Intro sign-ups | 10  | 5   | 4   |
| New members (40%) | 4   | 2   | 1.6 |
| Cost per new member | $150 | $300 | $375 |
| Lifetime value of those members | $2,880 | $1,440 | $1,152 |

All three still beat $600 of spend in this example, which is the point: the break-even is about one member (600 / 720 = 0.83). The danger is not click price. It is the sign-up rate. Scenario C costs the same media money as A and returns 60% fewer members.

Fix the page before you raise the budget. If your own lifetime value is $240, even scenario A (4 x $240 = $960) is thin, so do your own multiplication first.

## Why Yoga Studios Use Google Ads

Ads work best alongside:

*   A complete Google Business Profile (hours, photos, class types, reviews).
*   A landing page that makes booking an intro class easy.
*   Tracking that counts calls, form fills and booking-software sign-ups.

Ads send people to your profile and your website, so run our [Google Business Profile checklist](https://datalatte.pro/blog/google-business-profile-optimization-checklist) first.

Want a free review of your Google presence?

Send your business name. I reply with a short action plan within 48 hours.

[Get my free audit](https://datalatte.pro/free-audit)

## How to Set Up the Campaign

### Step 1: Choose Search

Start with a **Search campaign**, which shows your ad when someone types a relevant query. Consider Performance Max later, once you have conversion data and good landing pages.

### Step 2: Define your area and schedule

Google Ads lets you target a radius around a location ([Google Ads Help](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/1722038), checked Oct 2026). Tighter in a dense city, wider in a rural area.

Google's default, recommended setting ("Presence or interest") reaches people likely to be in, or regularly in, your target area as well as people who have shown interest in it; the "Presence" option limits this to people likely to be in or regularly in it, which suits a studio that serves only local residents.

Check when calls and bookings arrive and weight budget toward those hours.

### Step 3: Build keyword groups

Group by theme: beginner classes, hot yoga, prenatal yoga, yoga for back pain. Examples:

*   "beginner yoga classes \[city\]"
*   "yoga near me"
*   "hot yoga \[neighborhood\]"
*   "prenatal yoga \[city\]"
*   "yoga for back pain \[city\]"
*   "yoga studio intro offer"

Start with phrase and exact match. More ideas in [best Google Ads keywords for yoga studios](https://datalatte.pro/blog/best-google-ad-keywords-for-yoga-studios-in-2026).

### Step 4: Add negative keywords

Negative keywords exclude searches you do not want to pay for ([Google Ads Help](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2453972), checked Oct 2026). Starters: "yoga pants", "yoga mat", "yoga teacher training" (unless you offer it), "yoga jobs", "free yoga videos", "yoga poses pdf", and "yoga retreat" (if you do not run them). Read the Search terms report weekly to find more ([Google Ads Help](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2472708), checked Oct 2026).

## Write Ads a First-Timer Answers

Lead with an offer, a location and easy booking.

*   "Beginner Yoga in \[City\] | First Class Free" (only if you offer it)
*   "Book an Intro Class Online"
*   "All Levels Welcome. Small Classes."
*   "Yoga for Back Pain and Stress Relief"

Answer the hesitations: "No experience needed", "Mats provided", "Cancel anytime". Add a call asset so mobile searchers can phone from the ad ([Google Ads Help](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2453991), checked Oct 2026). Claim only the reviews and awards you can show.

## Budget: Work Backward

No source gives a yoga-specific ad budget, so use your own numbers:

1.  Lifetime value of a new student = monthly price x months they typically stay.
2.  The most you can pay to win one student and stay profitable.
3.  Monthly budget divided by that number = the new students you need to break even.

Check Keyword Planner for click costs, set a daily budget that buys enough clicks to learn from, and run it at least 60 days. If the numbers fail at your current sign-up rate, fix the page and offer first. For the wider picture, see our [local marketing budget guide](https://datalatte.pro/blog/local-marketing-budget-guide).

## Landing Page Basics

Send clicks to a page that matches the search, not the homepage. Include:

*   A headline for the offer (intro class, trial week, beginner series).
*   Schedule, price, address and phone number.
*   A one-tap booking button ab

[Keyword research is really about understanding people](https://wildheartmedia.com/keyword-research-yoga-retreats/#t-1792080469935)

[How Wildheart can help](https://wildheartmedia.com/keyword-research-yoga-retreats/#t-1792152229129)

* * *

### **Join the Mindful Marketing Movement**

[join now](https://wildheartmedia.com/mindful-marketing-movement/)

You've planned a beautiful yoga retreat. You've found the perfect venue, created a thoughtful programme and put together a website that captures the experience you're offering.

But there's one important question: **how will people find it?**

You might be sharing your retreat through your email list, word of mouth or social media. These can all help, but what about the people who don't know you yet? The ones who are actively searching for a retreat just like yours?

This is where keyword research comes in.

And the good news? You don't need expensive software or technical expertise to get started.

In this guide, we'll show you how to find the right keywords for your yoga retreat using free tools, understand what your potential guests are searching for and use those insights to make your retreat easier to discover online.

## What is keyword research (and why does it matter for retreats)?

[Keyword research](https://wildheartmedia.com/seo-for-wellbeing-businesses/) is the process of discovering the words and phrases people type into search engines when they're looking for something.

For a yoga retreat host, this might include:

*   Yoga retreat in Portugal
*   Beginners yoga retreat UK
*   Yoga and meditation retreat in India
*   Women's yoga retreat in Spain
*   Ashtanga yoga retreat in Greece

These are all examples of **_search queries_**: the actual phrases people enter into Google.

Keyword research helps you understand which queries are relevant to your retreat, so you can use the same language on your website.

This is an important part of [search engine optimisation](https://wildheartmedia.com/organic-search-why-is-seo-important/) (SEO), which is simply the process of helping search engines understand your website and show it to people who are looking for what you offer.

But there's a distinction worth making.

**The aim isn't to attract as many website visitors as possible. It's to attract the right visitors.**

A hundred people looking for a free yoga video aren't particularly useful if you're trying to fill a week-long retreat in Tuscany. Ten people actively researching yoga retreats in Tuscany could be much more valuable.

It's about relevance, not just numbers.

## Step 1: Start with your ideal retreat guest

Before opening Google or looking at keyword tools, think about the person you're trying to reach.

**Who is your retreat really for?**

Perhaps you're running an intensive Ashtanga yoga retreat for experienced practitioners. Or maybe you're offering a gentle yoga and meditation retreat for beginners who need some time away from everyday life.

These are very different experiences, and people will search for them differently.

Ask yourself:

*   Who would benefit most from this retreat?
*   What style of yoga or wellbeing practices are you offering?
*   Where is the retreat taking place?
*   Is it suitable for beginners or experienced practitioners?
*   What makes this experience different from other retreats?
*   What might someone be hoping to gain from attending?

For example, someone looking for an intensive Ashtanga retreat might search for 'traditional Ashtanga yoga retreat', while someone new to yoga might search for 'relaxing yoga retreat for beginners'.

Neither is necessarily better. They're simply different audiences.

At Wildheart, we always start with this kind of clarity before working on SEO. If you don't understand who you're trying to reach, it's difficult to know which keywords are worth targeting.

### Put it into practice

Write down 5-10 phrases you think your ideal guests might search for. Don't worry about getting them right yet. This is your starting list.

![Keyword research for retreat hosts: Start with your ideal guest](https://wildheartmedia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/keyword-research-yoga-retreats-1.webp "Step 1: Start with your ideal retreat guest")

## Step 2: Use Google to discover what people are searching for

One of the simplest keyword research tools is the search engine itself.

And it's free.

### Google autocomplete

Start typing one of your phrases into Google, but don't press Enter straight away.

Google may suggest additional searches based on what people commonly look for.

For example, start with:

'yoga retreat in'

You might see suggestions for particular countries, regions or destinations.

Try adding other words:

*   Yoga retreat for...
*   Yoga retreat with...
*   Yoga retreat beginners...
*   Meditation retreat in...

These suggestions can help you discover phrases you hadn't considered.

However, remember that autocomplete suggestions can vary depending on your location,

### [What Fitness Trainers and Instructors Do](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/fitness-trainers-and-instructors.htm#tab-2)

Fitness trainers and instructors lead, instruct, and motivate individuals or groups in exercise activities.

### [Work Environment](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/fitness-trainers-and-instructors.htm#tab-3)

Fitness trainers and instructors work in facilities such as recreation centers, health clubs, and yoga studios. Many work variable or part-time schedules that may include nights, weekends, or holidays.

### [How to Become a Fitness Trainer or Instructor](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/fitness-trainers-and-instructors.htm#tab-4)

The education and training typically required for fitness trainers and instructors varies by type of specialty, and employers prefer to hire those with certification.

### [Pay](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/fitness-trainers-and-instructors.htm#tab-5)

The median annual wage for fitness trainers and instructors was $47,160 in May 2025.

### [Job Outlook](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/fitness-trainers-and-instructors.htm#tab-6)

Employment of fitness trainers and instructors is projected to grow 7 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations.

About 68,000 openings for fitness trainers and instructors are projected each year, on average, over the decade. Many of those openings are expected to result from the need to replace workers who transfer to different occupations or exit the labor force, such as to retire.

Learn more about fitness trainers and instructors by visiting additional resources, including O*NET, a source on key characteristics of workers and occupations.

## What Fitness Trainers and Instructors Do[About this section](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/fitness-trainers-and-instructors.htm#TB_inline?height=325&width=325&inlineId=about-what-they-do)

![Image 1: Fitness trainers and instructors](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/images/2740.jpg)

Fitness trainers and instructors work with people of all ages and skill levels.

Fitness trainers and instructors lead, instruct, and motivate individuals or groups in exercise activities, including cardiovascular workouts (for the heart and blood circulation), strength training, and stretching. They work with people of all ages and skill levels.

### Duties

Fitness trainers and instructors typically do the following:

*   Demonstrate or explain how to perform various exercises and routines to minimize injuries and improve fitness
*   Watch clients do exercises to ensure that they are using correct technique
*   Provide options during workouts to help clients feel successful
*   Monitor clients’ progress and adapt programs as needed
*   Explain and enforce safety rules and regulations on sports, recreational activities, and the use of exercise equipment
*   Give clients information or resources about topics such as nutrition and lifestyle
*   Give emergency first aid if needed

_Fitness trainers and instructors_ work with individual clients or prepare or choreograph their own group classes. They may do a variety of tasks in addition to their fitness duties, such as managing the front desk, signing up new members, giving tours of the facility, or supervising the weight-training and cardiovascular equipment areas. Fitness trainers and instructors also may promote their facilities and instruction through social media, by writing newsletters or blog posts, or by creating posters and flyers.

**_Exercise trainers_**, also known as _personal fitness trainers_, work with individual clients or small groups. They may train in a gym or in clients’ homes. They evaluate their clients’ current fitness level, personal goals, and skills. Then, they develop personalized training programs for their clients to follow and monitor the clients’ progress. In gyms or other fitness facilities, these workers often sell training sessions to members.

**_Group fitness instructors_** organize and lead group exercise classes, which may include cardiovascular exercises, muscle strengthening, or stretching. Some instructors create a routine or select exercises for participants to follow, and they then choose music that is appropriate to the movement. Others teach prechoreographed routines that were created by fitness companies or organizations. They may lead classes that use specific exercise equipment, such as stationary bicycles; teach a specific conditioning method, such as yoga; or instruct specific age groups, such as seniors or youths.
